title: Server Errors and Consistent API Responses
summary: Distinguish expected client errors from unexpected server failures and return safe, consistent JSON.

sketchBlocks.title: Expected client errors differ from unexpected exceptions

tryItExercises.title: Protect a report route
tryItExercises.prompt: Implement `GET /api/summary` with `try/catch`. Call `buildSummary()`, return it with status `200`, and on an exception log a short server-side message then return status `500` JSON `{ error: "Internal server error" }`.
tryItExercises.hint: Keep internal exception details out of the JSON response.

help.concept: Unexpected failures should produce a safe client response while diagnostics stay server-side.
help.hint_1: Put the normal response path inside the try block.
help.hint_2: The catch may log details but should send only the stable public message.

sketchBlocks.title: A focused helper can reuse one error JSON shape

tryItExercises.title: Reuse one error response shape
tryItExercises.prompt: Create `sendError(res, status, message)` returning `{ error: message }`. Use it in `GET /api/rooms/:id` so a missing room returns `404` with `Room not found`; a found room returns status `200` JSON.
tryItExercises.hint: Keep lookup logic in the route and response formatting in the helper.

help.concept: A focused response helper removes repeated formatting without hiding domain decisions.
help.hint_1: The helper accepts the response object, status, and public message.
help.hint_2: The route still performs the lookup and chooses when to use the helper.

sourceChecks.message: Use the helper for a missing room.

quizDraft.title: Choose the unexpected-failure response
quizDraft.prompt: Which client response is appropriate when an unexpected exception escapes normal route logic?
quizDraft.hint: Choose the safe public outcome rather than exposing implementation details.

help.concept: Unexpected failures need a stable public response and private diagnostics.
help.hint_1: Do not expose stack traces to clients.
help.hint_2: The server may log details internally while returning a generic body.

options: A safe server-error status with a generic JSON message.
A success status with the stack trace.
A validation status for every exception.
A redirect to a debugging website.

quizDraft.title: Distinguish error categories
quizDraft.prompt: Which two outcomes are expected client-facing branches rather than unexpected server failures?
quizDraft.hint: Choose cases the route can deliberately recognize and explain.

help.concept: Expected API errors are part of the contract and should not be treated like crashes.
help.hint_1: One correct choice concerns invalid submitted data.
help.hint_2: Another concerns a lookup with no match.

options: A requested resource id does not exist.
A helper throws an unanticipated exception.
The process encounters an unknown defect.

quizDraft.title: Complete the unexpected failure response
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the status used for an unexpected server-side failure in this module.
quizDraft.hint: Choose the option representing an internal failure rather than a correctable client problem.

help.concept: This outcome is separate from validation and missing-resource branches.
help.hint_1: The public response should remain generic and safe.

quizDraft.template: When an unanticipated exception reaches the route's failure boundary, the API returns HTTP status [blank1].

quizDraft.title: Order unexpected error handling
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange the route behavior for an unexpected exception.
quizDraft.hint: Internal details may be logged after the failure is caught, but should not be sent to the client.

help.concept: Unexpected failures move from protected work to private diagnostics and a safe public response.
help.hint_2: Finish with the stable client-facing error.

tokens: Return a safe generic JSON error
